title: What makes it fast and accurate

cards.title: A PSP core built from scratch
cards.lead_md: It's written in ares's style from PSP docs, tests and real PSP measurements, with no code from other PSP emulators. PPSSPP was only a reference.
points_md: No firmware needed, since Phobos emulates the PSP's system software.
The CPU runs through a recompiler on ARM64 and x86-64, with an interpreter behind it.
Three renderers, with Vulkan going up to 10x the PSP's 480x272.
ISO, CSO, ZSO, DAX, JSO and CHD discs open as they are, and save states keep loading across builds.
cards.alt: God of War: Ghost of Sparta's main menu at 4x

cards.title: Timed against a real PSP-1000
cards.lead_md: Since 19 October, the PSP's graphics chip (the GE) takes about as long as my PSP-1000 did on the same work (#269). "Fast" still gives you Sony's peak rates.
points_md: Later rounds measured how the PSP's CPU slows the GE (#279, #291).
Real games captured on the same PSP check the result (#291).
Any timing change runs against all 266 test games before it merges.

cards.title: The GE on a separate thread
cards.lead_md: The GE's front end can run on a separate thread beside the emulated CPU, with identical results.
points_md: With it on, Killzone's emulation thread drops from 149 to 74 million host instructions a frame (#272, #277).
It's off by default. The app's "PSP Graphics Overlap" switch is built, and shows up once On beats Off on my RP6.

cards.title: A fast N64, even on the stock driver
cards.lead_md: It's ares's N64 core on parallel-RDP and Vulkan, with the recompilers tuned for ARM64.
points_md: It has 1x to 4x upscaling, the 64DD, Rumble and Controller Paks, and Turnip drivers from the app's GPU Driver Manager.
Since 21 October, N64 games also run on the RP6's stock Qualcomm driver, at a median 59.9 fps in the four games checked (#292).

compare.alt_after: Ocarina of Time after the fix, at 59.9 fps

cards.title: Full speed on a handheld
cards.lead_md: Measured along the way on my Retroid Pocket 6, a Snapdragon 8 Gen 2 handheld.
points_md: The 5x runs are two minutes from launch, so they're mostly logos, intros and menus.
On 6 October, drawing on several threads took the software renderer from 10.6 to 60 fps on Peace Walker's title screen.
cards.alt: F-Zero X at 59.9 fps on a Retroid Pocket 6

cards.title: Made for controllers, with lots of themes
cards.lead_md: The D-pad and stick move a visible focus, and the shoulder buttons switch tabs (#51). Touch controls get a layout per system.
points_md: 13 themes, like Dracula, Monokai, Rosé Pine and Synthwave '84, plus glass, retrowave neon and an XMB-style backdrop. The default, Phobos, is in this site's colours (#314).
A performance overlay, and control remapping per game, per console or for everything.
Screenshots pop out as a film-strip card and hop into a folder (#273).

cards.title: It updates itself
cards.lead_md: Settings → About updates the app from GitHub, from tagged releases or nightlies.
points_md: Build numbers come from git history, locally and on CI.
